messages:
jess.k: Heads-up — hit a flaky case where a phone switching from Wi-Fi to cellular mid-upload leads to OkHttp replaying the request on the new connection and the server getting a partial + full payload. Behavior seems tied to retryOnConnectionFailure and our Authenticator flow. Repro notes below.

jess.k: Repro: Pixel 4a emulator with simulated wifi->cell network change, OkHttp 4.10, Retrofit 2.9, uploading ~8MB file via streaming RequestBody. App uses Authenticator to refresh 401s and an application interceptor to attach Authorization header from TokenProvider.

mohit.r: Interesting. Network handoff can produce a socket exception that OkHttp classifies as recoverable and will re-enqueue the call on a new connection if retryOnConnectionFailure=true. For streaming bodies that are not replayable this can lead to duplicate server work if the first stream reached the server before the client saw the error.

sara.l: Did you see any differences between Android versions or HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1? H2 might multiplex but wifi->cell will usually drop the TCP connection entirely.

jess.k: We saw it more on Android 11 emulators, and reproduces reliably when we toggle network quickly during upload. With default client (retryOnConnectionFailure=true) server sometimes logged a 206 partial followed by 200 for same upload id.

tom.p: Two angles to mitigate: (1) avoid automatic replay for non-replayable bodies (retryOnConnectionFailure=false) for upload clients, (2) make uploads idempotent (upload-id / chunked resume) so duplicates are safe. Also ensure Authenticator refresh isn't racing across handoffs.

mohit.r: Another pattern: use a network interceptor to add Authorization header right before network I/O. That reduces window where a stale header might be attached to a replayed request caused by a new connection. But note network interceptors run after caching layer and at a lower level; picking application vs network interceptor has tradeoffs.

jess.k: Example change we tried:
```
val uploadClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(false)
  .connectionPool(ConnectionPool(0, 1, TimeUnit.SECONDS))
  .build()
```
This stopped the duplicate in our toggles, but we don't want to change default for everyone.

sara.l: For SDK guidance: add an "uploads" sample client with those settings and a small RequestBody helper that buffers <4MB. Also document the wifi->cell handoff caveat.

mohit.r: One more gotcha — if TokenProvider.refresh triggers a synchronous HTTP call on the same shared client, you can deadlock/queue on reconnection; prefer a dedicated refreshClient or offload refresh to a separate executor.

jess.k: We implemented: 1) uploadClient preset in samples with retry disabled, 2) network interceptor for auth header so header is fetched as late as possible, 3) aria-style upload-id header to let server dedupe. Re-runs dropped the problem to zero in our tests.

tom.p: Nice. Can we add a short lint/log in the SDK sample builder that warns when building a client with retryOnConnectionFailure=true and a RequestBody with unknown contentLength() (likely streaming)? That should help apps catch the mismatch early.

qa-bot: test-run 2311002600: wifi-handoff-upload (jess.k) -> flaky(8/10) before presets, 0/10 after uploadClient + network-interceptor + upload-id.

jess.k: I'll open a PR with: (A) sample uploadClient preset, (B) network-interceptor auth example, (C) docs section "Mobile network handoff and non-replayable uploads" and (D) a small buffered RequestBody helper (warning about memory). Thanks all :)
